info.title: Bilhikma Platform API
info.description:
REST API for the Bilhikma learning platform: student registration and approval, entity/class/subject structure, protected lesson delivery, textbooks, live sessions, notifications and the administration dashboard.

## Conventions

- Every response — success or failure — is wrapped in the same envelope: `{ "data": ..., "message": "...", "status_code": 0|1 }`. `status_code` is a logical flag (1 = success, 0 = failure) and is independent of the HTTP status, which always stays protocol-correct.
- Lists return `data.items` plus `data.meta.pagination` (`count`, `current_page`, `per_page`, `total`). An empty list is a success with `items: []`, never an error.
- Validation failures return HTTP 422 with `errors` — an object keyed by field name, each holding an array of message strings.
- Send `Accept: application/json` on every request. Without it Laravel may answer with an HTML error page instead of the JSON envelope.
- Send `Accept-Language: ar` or `en` to choose the language of `message` and `errors`. Arabic is the default for the mobile app.
- Authenticated requests carry `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. Tokens are bound to one device: logging in elsewhere revokes the previous session, and the next request from it returns 401.

## Getting started

1. Import `bilhikma-api.postman_environment.json` and select it.
2. Set `base_url` to your server.
3. Run **Authentication → Log in (admin)** once. The access and refresh tokens
   are captured automatically — nothing needs to be pasted by hand.
4. Run **Authentication → Log in (student)** to work through the app endpoints.

Ids are captured as you go: listing entities stores `entity_id`, listing lessons
stores `content_id`, and so on. Requests further down the collection reference
those variables, so a folder can be run top to bottom without editing anything.

> The API allows one active session per account. Logging in as the student
> revokes the admin session and vice versa, so keep the two tokens in separate
> variables — which is exactly what this collection does
> (`access_token` and `admin_token`).

get.description:
Populates the first dropdown on the registration screen.

Only entities that are both active and currently accepting registrations are returned. An entity the administration has archived or closed simply disappears from this list, so the app never offers a choice the next request would reject.

### Captured into the environment

- `{{entity_id}}` ← `data.items[0].id`

example.message: Entities open for registration fetched successfully.

get.description:
Populates the second dropdown, linked to the entity just chosen.

Returned as a tree, because classes nest (stage → level → term) and only the leaves can be registered into. Use `is_selectable` to decide which rows are tappable: a parent node is a grouping header, not a class a student can join.

### Path parameters

- `entity` — *integer*, required. Entity id taken from the previous call.

### Captured into the environment

- `{{category_id}}` ← `data.items[0].children[0].children[0].id`

get.description:
Reference list behind the nationality and country-of-residence dropdowns.

One list serves both dropdowns. A row carries the country under two readings: `name` answers "where do you live" and `nationality` answers "what is your nationality", so the form fetches this once and reads the field each control needs. 

Ordering comes from the server and is deliberate: Syria first, then the rest of the Arab League, then everyone else alphabetically by Arabic name. Render the list in the order it arrives rather than re-sorting it. 

Registration validates `nationality` and `country_of_residence` against this list. Any of `code`, `name`, `name_en`, `nationality` or `nationality_en` identifies a row, so the app may send whichever field it holds. `dial_code` is included because the same form asks for a WhatsApp number with its international code.

post.description:
Creates the account, the student profile and a pending enrollment request.

Multipart, because five supporting documents are uploaded with the form. The account is created immediately but reaches no content: the enrollment starts as `pending` and a supervisor has to approve it. Rate limited to 5 requests/minute. 

The body mirrors the institution admission form in full. Two fields are conditional rather than always required: `prior_studies_details` becomes required when `has_prior_islamic_studies` is true, and `quran_memorization_note` becomes required when `quran_memorization_level` is `partial`. Both are discarded when their condition does not hold, so a later change of answer cannot leave stale text on the record. 

`whatsapp_number` is deliberately separate from `phone`: the institution contacts applicants on WhatsApp and the two are frequently different numbers. Send it with the international dialling code. 

`nationality` and `country_of_residence` are validated against the reference list served by `GET /public/countries`. Send any of that row's `code`, `name`, `name_en`, `nationality` or `nationality_en` - all five identify the same country. A value outside the list is rejected. `city` remains free text.

### Body fields

- `full_name` — *string*, **required**. Student's full name as it should appear on certificates and on the textbook watermark. Max 200.
- `phone` — *string*, **required**. Primary login identifier. Must be unique across the platform. Max 30.
- `email` — *email*, **required**. Second login identifier and the destination for OTP codes. Must be unique.
- `password` — *string*, **required**. At least 8 characters, with an upper-case letter, a lower-case letter, a digit and a symbol.
- `password_confirmation` — *string*, **required**. Must match `password` exactly.
- `gender` — *enum*, **required**. `male` or `female`.
- `date_of_birth` — *date*, **required**. Format YYYY-MM-DD. Must be in the past.
- `father_name` — *string*, **required**. Father's name. Max 200.
- `mother_name` — *string*, **required**. Mother's name. Max 200.
- `kunya` — *string*, optional. Optional teknonym (e.g. أبو محمد). Max 200.
- `nationality` — *string*, **required**. Nationality, from `GET /public/countries`. Accepts the row's code, name or demonym in either language. Max 100.
- `country_of_residence` — *string*, **required**. Country the applicant currently lives in - separate from nationality. From `GET /public/countries`, same accepted forms. Max 100.
- `city` — *string*, **required**. City of residence. Max 100.
- `whatsapp_number` — *string*, **required**. WhatsApp number with the international dialling code. The institution contacts applicants on this number, and it may differ from `phone`. Max 30.
- `telegram_handle` — *string*, optional. Telegram username, if any. Max 100.
- `specialization` — *string*, **required**. Academic or professional specialisation. Max 200.
- `education_level` — *enum*, **required**. `school`, `secondary`, `university_student`, `university_graduate` or `postgraduate`.
- `has_prior_islamic_studies` — *boolean*, **required**. Whether the applicant has previously studied Islamic or Arabic sciences.
- `prior_studies_details` — *string*, optional. Which texts or subjects were studied. Required when `has_prior_islamic_studies` is true; ignored otherwise. Max 2000.
- `quran_memorization_level` — *enum*, **required**. `none`, `partial` or `complete`.
- `quran_memorization_note` — *string*, optional. Which parts are memorised. Required when `quran_memorization_level` is `partial`; ignored otherwise. Max 255.
- `entity_id` — *integer*, **required**. Entity being applied to. Must be active and open for registration.
- `category_id` — *integer*, **required**. Class within that entity. Must be a leaf class and belong to `entity_id`.
- `identity` — *file*, **required**. Passport or national ID. jpg/png/pdf, max 5 MB.
- `photo` — *file*, **required**. Personal photograph. jpg/png, max 2 MB.
- `cv` — *file*, **required**. Curriculum vitae. PDF only, max 5 MB.
- `qualification[]` — *file[]*, **required**. Academic qualifications — at least one, repeat the field for more. jpg/png/pdf, max 5 MB each.
- `recommendation` — *file*, **required**. Letter of recommendation from a recognised body. jpg/png/pdf, max 5 MB.

### Captured into the environment

- `{{student_id}}` ← `data.student.id`
- `{{enrollment_id}}` ← `data.enrollment.id`

post.description:
The same endpoint, used with an administrator email — run this first to work the dashboard folders.

Administrators authenticate with email; the phone channel is reserved for students and is rejected for an admin account. The dashboard sends no `device_uuid` or `platform` — those belong to the mobile app, where one active session per account is enforced against the installation id. An administrator session is recorded as `web`. 

                    The Postman collection stores the resulting token in `admin_token`, separate from the student `access_token`, because the platform allows one active session per account and the two flows are exercised side by side.

### Body fields

- `email` — *email*, **required**. Administrator email address.
- `password` — *string*, **required**. Minimum 6 characters.

Trades a refresh token for a new access token without re-entering credentials.

Backs the "remember me" checkbox. The refresh token rotates on every call — store the new one and discard the old, which stops working immediately. 

                    **Send the expiring access token as the Bearer header as well.** The server needs it to identify which device session to move onto the new token; omit it and the session keeps expecting the old token, so the freshly issued one is rejected on the very next request.

### Body fields

- `refresh_token` — *string*, **required**. The refresh token from the last login or refresh.

### Captured into the environment

- `{{student_token}}` ← `data.access_token`
- `{{access_token}}` ← `data.access_token`
- `{{refresh_token}}` ← `data.refresh_token`

Sends a 6-digit OTP over WhatsApp, SMS or email.

The channel is chosen from the identifier: an email address is always mailed, a phone number goes to whichever phone channel is configured. Pass `channel` to override — e.g. start from a phone number but receive the code by email. The response is byte-for-byte identical whether or not the account exists, so this cannot be used to enumerate users. The code is valid for 10 minutes and dies after 5 wrong attempts. Rate limited to 6 requests/minute.

### Body fields

- `identifier` — *string*, **required**. Phone number or email address. `phone` and `email` are also accepted as aliases.
- `channel` — *enum*, optional. `whatsapp`, `sms` or `email`. Omit to let the server pick.

example.message: A verification code has been sent to your email.

post.description:
Checks the code without consuming it, so the next screen can proceed.

A read-only check: the code stays usable for the reset call that follows. It is only burned once the new password is submitted.

### Body fields

- `identifier` — *string*, **required**. The same identifier used to request the code.
- `code` — *string*, **required**. The 6-digit code.

post.description:
Consumes the code and replaces the password.

Every active session and refresh token for the account is revoked, on every device — a password reset must not leave a stale session alive. The code cannot be reused afterwards.

### Body fields

- `identifier` — *string*, **required**. The same identifier used to request the code.
- `code` — *string*, **required**. The 6-digit code.
- `password` — *string*, **required**. Minimum 6 characters.
- `password_confirmation` — *string*, **required**. Must match `password`.

get.description:
Everything the side drawer renders: entities, their class trees, and which class is selected.

The tree is pruned to the student's own enrollments — an entity's full structure is never exposed here. Ancestors are included so a leaf can be drawn under its stage, but only nodes carrying an `enrollment_id` are tappable. Classes the student has been transferred out of appear with `status: "archived"`; they stay readable so a student can revisit a level they have finished.

### Captured into the environment

- `{{active_enrollment_id}}` ← `data.active_enrollment_id`

The selected entity and class on their own — enough to draw the app header.

Cheaper than fetching the whole drawer when only the header needs redrawing.

put.description:
Points the whole app at a different entity or class.

After this call every student listing — lessons, textbooks, albums, live sessions, notifications — returns the new class's content and nothing else. The two entities are never blended into one list. The choice persists on the server, so it survives a reinstall or a device change. An `enrollment_id` belonging to another student returns 403 and is recorded as an unauthorised-access event — not 422 — so the endpoint cannot be used to probe which ids exist.

### Body fields

- `enrollment_id` — *integer*, **required**. One of the ids from `/user/my-enrollments`. Must belong to the caller and be `approved` or `archived`.

### Captured into the environment

- `{{active_enrollment_id}}` ← `data.enrollment_id`

This enrollment is not available to you.

get.description:
Everything the home screen shows: header, overall progress, resume card and subject tiles.

One call for the whole screen. `context` carries the entity logo and class name for the header; `summary` is the overall progress ring and the subject/lesson counters; `resume` is the "continue where you left off" card — null when there is nothing part-finished; `items` are the subject tiles with their own progress bars. A student whose enrollment is still pending gets `context: null` and an empty list rather than an error.

### Captured into the environment

- `{{category_subject_id}}` ← `data.items[0].category_subject_id`

One subject with its progress, a count per tab and its current textbooks.

The six tabs are lectures, audio, articles, image albums, live sessions and textbooks. A zero count means the tab should be shown disabled rather than hidden. A subject may publish several textbooks at once (a main text plus a workbook, say), which is why `textbooks` is a list.

### Path parameters

- `categorySubject` — *integer*, required. The `category_subject_id` from the home screen tiles.

get.description:
Published lessons in the currently selected class.

Scoped entirely from the token and the drawer selection — passing a class or entity id has no effect, and filtering by one is rejected. Each item carries the caller's own progress, so a list screen can draw progress bars without a second call.

### Query parameters

- `filter[category_subject_id]` — *integer*, optional. Narrow to one subject.
- `filter[type]` — *enum*, optional. `video`, `audio` or `article`. Backs the subject screen tabs.
- `search` — *string*, optional. Free-text match on the lesson title and description. Backs the search screen.
- `sort` — *string*, optional. `order` (default) or `published_at`. Prefix with `-` to reverse.
- `page` — *integer*, optional. Page number. Default 1.
- `per_page` — *integer*, optional. Items per page. Default 15.

### Captured into the environment

- `{{content_id}}` ← `data.items[0].id`

get.description:
One lesson with its attachments, its article body and the caller's progress.

This is the only endpoint that returns `article_body`, and only for an unlocked lesson. It also adds `subject_name` and `attachments`, neither of which appears in the listing. 

                            A locked lesson returns 403 because the previous lesson in the same subject has not been completed. Show the `message` from the body; it is already localised. 

                            Requesting a lesson from a class the student is not enrolled in returns 403 and writes a security event recording the student, the lesson, the device and the app version. Lessons from a class the student has finished stay readable.

### Path parameters

- `content` — *integer*, required. Lesson id.

example.message: Finish the previous lesson to unlock this one.

post.description:
Mints a temporary, device-bound link for the video or audio file.

Call this immediately before playback and hand the returned token to the player as `GET /api/media/{token}?device_uuid=...`. The link is bound to `device_uuid`: copied to another device it returns 403 and is recorded as a device conflict. It is reusable until it expires (default 3 days, configurable) so pausing and resuming works. 

A locked lesson is refused here too, and the refusal is written to the security-event log. This is the gate that makes sequential access a rule rather than a client-side convention: without a token there is no playable URL for any client to fetch.

### Path parameters

- `content` — *integer*, required. Lesson id. Must be a video or audio lesson.

### Body fields

- `device_uuid` — *string*, **required**. Must match the device_uuid used at login, or the link will not work.

### Captured into the environment

- `{{media_token}}` ← `data.token`

example.message: Finish the previous lesson to unlock this one.

post.description:
Records how far the student has watched, and refuses forward seeking.

Called four times per lesson, not on a timer. The player counts locally and reports only when it crosses one of the positions in `checkpoints` (25%, 50%, 75% and 100% of the duration). A two-hour lesson therefore costs four writes per student instead of roughly 2,400. 

Report the checkpoints in order and never two back to back: each one is measured against how much wall-clock time has actually passed, so a catch-up burst is read as a skip and rejected. 

A locked lesson returns 403 here as well. 

Forward seeking is refused **on the server**: a reported position may only advance as fast as real time has actually passed since the previous heartbeat. A jump returns 422 together with `allowed_position_seconds` — rewind the player to that point. 

`watched_delta_seconds` is validated, never trusted: claiming more playback than wall-clock time allows is capped silently. 

An article has no timeline. Posting `position_seconds: 0` against one marks it read - `progress_percent: 100`, `is_completed: true` - which is what unlocks the next lesson. The value sent is ignored for articles; zero is simply a neutral filler for a required field.

### Path parameters

- `content` — *integer*, required. Lesson id.

### Body fields

- `position_seconds` — *integer*, **required**. The checkpoint value being reported, in whole seconds. `0` for an article.
- `watched_delta_seconds` — *integer*, optional. Seconds actually played since the previous report - played duration, not the difference between positions. Optional in the schema, but omitting it makes the server derive attendance from position movement, which credits a rewatch as zero. Max 3600.

get.description:
Fetches the watermarked PDF. Run this straight after the request above.

The watermark is stamped at this moment, not in advance: the platform name, the student serial, the student name and the date run diagonally across every page in grey. 

                    The response is a PDF attachment, not JSON. In Postman use **Save Response - Save to a file** to open it. 

                    The link burns on use. Sending it a second time answers 403, and so does sending it from a different `device_uuid` - that one is also written to the security log as a device conflict. Both are correct behaviour, not faults: request a fresh link for every download.

### Path parameters

- `token` — *string*, required. Captured automatically from the request above.

### Query parameters

- `device_uuid` — *string*, required. Must match the device the link was issued to.

Single-use and short-lived (5 minutes by default) — it dies the moment the file is fetched.

Textbooks published for the currently selected class.

post.description:
Mints a single-use link to a freshly watermarked copy.

Textbooks are the one thing students are meant to keep — the file downloads as an attachment and can be saved to the device, unlike video. 

The watermark is generated at download time, so every copy is traceable to the student who took it. The link works exactly once and expires after 5 minutes; request a new one for each download. 

Follow up with `GET /api/media/{token}?device_uuid=...`.

### Path parameters

- `textbook` — *integer*, required. Textbook id.

### Body fields

- `device_uuid` — *string*, **required**. Must match the login device.

### Captured into the environment

- `{{textbook_token}}` ← `data.token`
- `{{media_token}}` ← `data.token`

- `per_page` — *integer*, optional. Default 15.

delete.description:
Closes the attendance record and freezes the total.

**This request deletes an existing record.** The id in the URL is 999999 — deliberately one that does not exist, so running this folder end to end cannot touch real data, and the request answers 404 until you point it somewhere. Put the id you actually mean in before sending.

### Path parameters

- `liveSession` — *integer*, required. Live session id.

post.description:
Keeps the attendance record alive while the stream is on screen.

Send every 30 to 60 seconds. This is what turns "tapped the link" into "was present for N minutes" — without it, a student who joined and closed the app is indistinguishable from one who stayed to the end. 

A YouTube player does not report its position to us, and for a live stream everyone is at the live edge anyway, so time present is the meaningful measure — not a playhead position.

### Path parameters

- `liveSession` — *integer*, required. Live session id.

get.description:
The in-app notification screen — the most recent 50.

Scoped to the entity currently selected in the drawer: switching entities switches which announcements are listed. `per_page` is capped at 50.

### Query parameters

- `per_page` — *integer*, optional. Default and maximum 50.

### Captured into the environment

- `{{notification_id}}` ← `data.items[0].id`

post.description:
Records that the caller has seen it.

Idempotent — calling it twice is harmless.

### Path parameters

- `notification` — *integer*, required. Notification id.

get.description:
The signed-in student own details, as shown on the profile screen.

The institution and academic path follow the drawer selection, so this screen agrees with whatever the rest of the app is scoped to rather than picking an arbitrary enrollment. Both are empty strings rather than null when there is no current enrollment, so the screen never renders the word null. 

`can_capture_screen` is also returned at login. It is repeated here so the app can pick up a granted or revoked screen-capture exemption on resume, without a new sign-in.

patch.description:
Edits the fields a student may change about themselves.

The phone number is deliberately not editable here: it is the login identity and the target for OTP delivery, so changing it is an account-recovery operation rather than a profile edit.

### Body fields

- `full_name` — *string*, optional. Max 255 characters.
- `email` — *string*, optional. Must be unique across accounts.

post.description:
Changes the password of the signed-in student.

The new password must satisfy the student password policy: at least 8 characters with an upper-case letter, a lower-case letter, a digit and a symbol. The same rule is enforced wherever a student password is set, including the admin dashboard.

### Body fields

- `current_password` — *string*, **required**. The password in use now.
- `new_password` — *string*, **required**. The new password. Must differ from the current one.
- `new_password_confirmation` — *string*, **required**. Must match `new_password`.

Files a new enrollment request from an existing account.

A student may hold approved enrollments in several entities at once and switch between them from the drawer. This is not a new registration: the account, phone and email are untouched, so no uniqueness check applies. 

Moving between classes **within** the same entity is a transfer performed by an administrator, not this endpoint.

### Body fields

- `entity_id` — *integer*, **required**. Target entity. Must be active and open for registration.
- `category_id` — *integer*, **required**. Target class. Must be a leaf class inside that entity.

You already have a pending enrollment request for this entity.

post.description:
Stores the FCM token on the current session and subscribes it to the student topics.

Notifications are addressed to topics - `entity_{id}` and `category_{id}` - not to individual devices, so a device that has never been subscribed receives nothing at all. Login subscribes automatically; call this whenever Firebase rotates the token afterwards. 

The token is stored against the active device session, so it is dropped when that session is revoked.

### Body fields

- `fcm_token` — *string*, **required**. The token from Firebase Messaging.
- `device_uuid` — *string*, **required**. Must match the device that is signed in.

Logs a screenshot, screen recording or external display detected by the app.

The app detects these locally — `userDidTakeScreenshotNotification` and `UIScreen.isCaptured` on iOS — and reports them here. 

The first screenshot also raises the first rung of the disciplinary ladder automatically. Three counted violations inside the configured window suspend the account immediately, in the same request: check `account_suspended` in the response and send the student back to the login screen when it is true. 

Only these three client-observable types are accepted. Server-side event types such as unauthorised access or token reuse are never taken from a client payload. 

An account holding a screen-capture exemption (the QA team) is treated differently: the event is still recorded in full, but it does not count toward the policy, raises no warning and can never suspend the account. Clears the violation counter and reopens an account the policy locked.

Three counted screen-capture violations inside the configured window suspend an account automatically. This endpoint undoes that in one call: the counter goes to zero, the warning ladder is cleared, any active automatic suspension is closed, and a suspended account is set back to `active`. 

Written for the QA team, who trip the rule while testing the very feature that enforces it. 

The security events are **not** deleted. They stay on file with `counts_toward_policy` set to false, so the record of what happened survives while its effect on the counter does not. `GET /admin/students/{student}/security-events` still lists them. 

The warning ladder is cleared as well, because a soft notice is issued only once per account for its lifetime - leaving it would make the next screenshot skip the first rung and land on a harsher one. 

A manual suspension is left alone. Only an account the policy itself locked is reopened; a supervisor decision is not something a violation reset should quietly undo - use the activation endpoint for that. 

Sessions are untouched: a signed-in student stays signed in. Every call is written to the audit log with the administrator, the counts and the reason.

### Path parameters

- `student` — *integer*, required. Student id.

### Body fields

- `reason` — *string*, optional. Why the reset was performed. Recorded in the audit log. Optional.
